description: Three-panel EIS figure for Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels labelled S0 (red stars), S950 (green circles), S1050 (blue triangles) and S1150 (pink squares), each with a black solid fitting line; no numeric data labels are printed on any panel. (a) Nyquist plot, -Z_im versus Z_re, both axes in Ω·cm² with ticks 0–8000 every 2000; an inset shows the two-time-constant equivalent circuit used for fitting (Rs in series with Q1 parallel to R1+(Q2‖R2)), and two arrows mark the 0.01 Hz end points of the arcs. S950 sweeps the largest capacitive arc (reaching about Z_re 6800, -Z_im 5100), S0 the smallest (about Z_re 4000, -Z_im 1700), and S1050/S1150 lie between (≈5700/3800 and ≈4700/2700), giving the ranking S950 > S1050 > S1150 > S0. (b) Bode magnitude, |Z| (Ω·cm²) versus Frequency (Hz), log–log axes 10^0–10^5 Ω·cm² and 10^−2–10^5 Hz: low-frequency |Z| for S950 sits just below the 10^4 gridline, lower for S1050, S1150 and S0, and all curves converge to a few Ω·cm² above 10^4 Hz. (c) Bode phase, -Phase (deg) versus Frequency (Hz), 0–80°: every sample peaks between the 60 and 80° gridlines near 5–10 Hz, and S950 retains a higher phase angle up to ~10^3 Hz while S0 falls earliest. The group demonstrates that the S950 oxide film is the most protective (highest R_p, 21355 Ω·cm²).

subfigures.description: Nyquist plot of -Z_im vs Z_re (both Ω·cm², 0–8000 gridlines) for S0, S950, S1050, S1150 with black fitting lines; inset equivalent circuit Rs + [Q1 ‖ (R1 + (Q2 ‖ R2))]; arrows annotate the 0.01 Hz end points. S950 has the largest, S0 the smallest capacitive arc radius.

Bode magnitude plot: |Z| (Ω·cm², 10^0–10^5) vs Frequency (Hz, 10^−2–10^5), log–log, same four samples plus fitting lines. Low-frequency impedance modulus is highest for S950 (just below 10^4 Ω·cm²) and decreases for the other samples; curves converge near a few Ω·cm² at the highest frequencies.

Bode phase plot: -Phase (deg, 0–80) vs Frequency (Hz, 10^−2–10^5), log x axis. All four samples peak between the 60 and 80° gridlines around 5–10 Hz; S950 keeps a higher phase angle over a wider frequency range and S0 drops off first, while S0 starts lowest at 10^−2 Hz.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a Nyquist plot with -Z_im and Z_re both plotted in Ω·cm² over 0–8000, and four data series labelled S0, S950, S1050, S1150 plus a 'fitting line' entry in the legend.
In panel (a) the green S950 curve has the largest capacitive arc and the red S0 curve the smallest, with S1050 and S1150 in between, so the arc radius ranking is S950 > S1050 > S1150 > S0.
Panel (a) contains an inset equivalent-circuit diagram labelled Rs, Q1, R1, Q2 and R2, arranged as Rs in series with Q1 in parallel with the branch R1 + (Q2‖R2), i.e. a two-time-constant model.
Arrows inside panel (a) point to the high-impedance end of the arcs and are annotated '0.01 Hz', marking the lowest measured frequency.
The largest arc in (a) terminates near Z_re ≈ 6800 Ω·cm² and -Z_im ≈ 5100 Ω·cm² (read against the 2000-interval gridlines), and the smallest near Z_re ≈ 4000 Ω·cm² and -Z_im ≈ 1700 Ω·cm².
Panel (b) is a Bode magnitude plot of |Z| (Ω·cm²) against Frequency (Hz) on log–log axes spanning 10^0–10^5 Ω·cm² and 10^−2–10^5 Hz.

In panel (b) the low-frequency impedance modulus is highest for S950 (just below the 10^4 Ω·cm² gridline) and lower for S1050, S1150 and S0, and all four curves converge to only a few Ω·cm² above 10^4 Hz.

Panel (c) is a Bode phase plot of -Phase (deg) versus Frequency (Hz) with a y-axis of 0–80° and a logarithmic x-axis of 10^−2–10^5 Hz; all four curves peak between the 60 and 80° gridlines at roughly 5–10 Hz.

In panel (c) S950 (green) retains an elevated phase angle to higher frequency than the other samples and S0 (red) shows the earliest and lowest drop-off, with S0 also starting from the lowest phase angle at 10^−2 Hz.

The caption states the EIS measurements were made on the LDSs after potentiostatic polarization for 7200 s in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, and that panels (a), (b), (c) are the Nyquist, Bode magnitude and Bode phase plots respectively.

The citing text reports that the S950 sample achieves the highest polarization resistance R_p of 21355 Ω·cm², obtained by fitting the equivalent circuit of Fig. 11a (results in Table 3); this number is not printed anywhere in the figure itself.

The citing text attributes the smallest capacitive arc of S0 to poorer protective performance of its oxide film and higher corrosion susceptibility, and states that the arc radius decreases with grain growth.
The citing text interprets panel (c) as showing that the S950 oxide film is more stable and uniform because it maintains a higher phase angle over a wider frequency range.

unreadable_items: panel (a): no numeric data labels; arc end-point values can only be read against the 2000-interval gridlines
panels (b) and (c): no printed numbers on curves; |Z| and phase values readable only to gridline precision
the peak phase-angle value in panel (c) is not printed (only that it lies between the 60 and 80° gridlines)
equivalent-circuit element values (Rs, Q1, R1, Q2, R2) are not printed in the figure
